problem.title: Гена, возьми определитель
problem.statement:
Найдите сумму всех положительных значений \(a\), при которых матрица
\[
A=\bigl(\min(i,j)\cdot a^{|i-j|}\bigr)_{i,j=1}^{2026}
\]
вырождена.
problem.solution:
Обозначим \(n=2026\).

Для \(i=n,n-1,\ldots,2\) заменим строку \(R_i\) на \(R_i-aR_{i-1}\). Исходная матрица
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1\cdot a^0&1\cdot a^1&1\cdot a^2&\cdots&1\cdot a^{n-1}\\
1\cdot a^1&2\cdot a^0&2\cdot a^1&\cdots&2\cdot a^{n-2}\\
1\cdot a^2&2\cdot a^1&3\cdot a^0&\cdots&3\cdot a^{n-3}\\
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
1\cdot a^{n-1}&2\cdot a^{n-2}&3\cdot a^{n-3}&\cdots&n\cdot a^0
\end{pmatrix}
\]
переходит в верхнетреугольную матрицу
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1\cdot a^0&1\cdot a^1&1\cdot a^2&\cdots&1\cdot a^{n-1}\\
0&(2-a^2)\cdot a^0&(2-a^2)\cdot a^1&\cdots&(2-a^2)\cdot a^{n-2}\\
0&0&(3-2a^2)\cdot a^0&\cdots&(3-2a^2)\cdot a^{n-3}\\
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
0&0&0&\cdots&(n-(n-1)a^2)\cdot a^0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

После этих преобразований определитель не поменялся, а матрица стала верхнетреугольной, поэтому
\[
\det A=\prod_{i=2}^{n}\bigl(i-(i-1)a^2\bigr).
\]
Отсюда
\[
a^2=\frac{i}{i-1}
\]
для некоторого \(i\in\{2,\ldots,n\}\). Следовательно, сумма всех положительных значений \(a\) равна
\[
\sum_{i=2}^{2026}\sqrt{\frac{i}{i-1}}\approx 2028.939215760406073.
\]

\[
A=\bigl(\min(i,j)\cdot a^{|i-j|}\bigr)_{i,j=1}^{2026}
\]
вырождена.

results.answer:
The matrix \(A\) is the \(n \times n\) matrix with \(n = 2026\) and entries
\[
a_{ij} = \min(i,j) \cdot a^{|i-j|}.
\]
The goal is to determine all positive real numbers \(a > 0\) such that \(A\) is singular and to compute their sum.

Let \(\alpha = a > 0\) and \(\beta = \alpha^2\). To determine when \(A\) is singular, solve the equation \(Ax = 0\) for \(x \in \mathbb{R}^n\) with \(x \neq 0\). Denote the components of \(Ax\) by
\[
s_i = \sum_{j=1}^i j \, \alpha^{i-j} x_j + i \sum_{j=i+1}^n \alpha^{j-i} x_j, \qquad i = 1, \dots, n.
\]
The vector \(x\) lies in the kernel of \(A\) if and only if \(s_i = 0\) for all \(i\).

Introduce the auxiliary quantities \(q_{n+1} = 0\) and
\[
q_i = x_i + \alpha q_{i+1}, \qquad i = n, \dots, 1
\]
(equivalently, \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\) for \(i = 1, \dots, n\)). These satisfy
\[
q_i = \sum_{j=i}^n \alpha^{j-i} x_j.
\]
The tail sum in the expression for \(s_i\) then simplifies to \(\sum_{j > i} \alpha^{j-i} x_j = \alpha q_{i+1}\), so that
\[
s_i = \sum_{j=1}^i j \, \alpha^{i-j} x_j + i \alpha q_{i+1}.
\]
Substitute \(x_j = q_j - \alpha q_{j+1}\) into the remaining sum. After collecting coefficients of the \(q_k\), the cross terms involving \(q_{i+1}\) cancel and one obtains
\[
s_i = \sum_{k=1}^i \bigl( k - (k-1)\beta \bigr) \alpha^{i-k} \, q_k.
\]
Denote \(c_k = k - (k-1)\beta\) and
\[
u_i = \sum_{k=1}^i c_k \, \alpha^{i-k} q_k.
\]
The equation \(Ax = 0\) is then equivalent to \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i = 1, \dots, n\).

The quantities \(u_i\) satisfy the forward recurrence
\[
u_i - \alpha u_{i-1} = c_i q_i \qquad (i \geq 2),
\]
with the convention \(u_0 = 0\). In particular,
\[
u_1 = c_1 q_1, \qquad c_1 = 1.
\]
Thus \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i\) forces \(c_i q_i = 0\) for all \(i = 1, \dots, n\). Conversely, if \(c_k q_k = 0\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, n\), then the recurrence together with \(u_1 = 0\) implies \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i\) by induction. Consequently, \(Ax = 0\) if and only if \(c_k q_k = 0\) for all \(k\), where the sequence \((q_i)\) determines \(x\) via \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\) and \(q_{n+1} = 0\).

A nontrivial kernel exists precisely when there exists a nontrivial sequence \((q_1, \dots, q_n)\) with \(q_{n+1} = 0\) satisfying \(q_k = 0\) whenever \(c_k \neq 0\) (the values \(q_k\) may be chosen freely at those indices where \(c_k = 0\)). Solving \(c_k = 0\) yields
\[
k - (k-1)\beta = 0 \iff \beta = \frac{k}{k-1}
\]
for integers \(k \geq 2\) (the case \(k = 1\) gives \(c_1 = 1 \neq 0\) independently of \(\beta\)). Therefore:

- If \(\beta = m/(m-1)\) for some integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\), then \(c_m = 0\). Choosing, for example, \(q_m = 1\) and \(q_k = 0\) for all \(k \neq m\) produces a nontrivial sequence \((q_i)\). The corresponding vector \(x\) (given by \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\)) is necessarily nonzero. Hence the kernel is nontrivial and \(A\) is singular.
- If \(\beta \neq m/(m-1)\) for every integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\), then \(c_k \neq 0\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, n\). The conditions \(c_k q_k = 0\) force \(q_k = 0\) for all \(k\), whence \(x = 0\). The kernel is trivial and \(A\) is nonsingular.

It follows that \(A\) is singular if and only if
\[
\alpha^2 = \frac{m}{m-1}
\]
for some integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\). Since \(\alpha > 0\), the positive values of \(a\) are exactly
\[
a_m = \sqrt{\frac{m}{m-1}}, \qquad m = 2, 3, \dots, 2026.
\]
These \(2025\) numbers are pairwise distinct. Their sum is
\[
\sum_{m=2}^{2026} \sqrt{\frac{m}{m-1}} = \sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}.
\]

For each such value the corresponding auxiliary sequence \((q_i)\) produces a nonzero vector \(x\) satisfying \(Ax = 0\), so the indicated values of \(a\) indeed render \(A\) singular. No other positive values of \(a\) produce a nontrivial kernel.

Thus the required sum is \(\sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}\).

Final answer: \(\sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}\)

The matrix \(A\) is the \(n \times n\) matrix with \(n = 2026\) and entries
\[
a_{ij} = \min(i,j) \cdot a^{|i-j|}.
\]
The goal is to determine all positive real numbers \(a > 0\) such that \(A\) is singular and to compute their sum.

Let \(\alpha = a > 0\) and \(\beta = \alpha^2\). To determine when \(A\) is singular, solve the equation \(Ax = 0\) for \(x \in \mathbb{R}^n\) with \(x \neq 0\). Denote the components of \(Ax\) by
\[
s_i = \sum_{j=1}^i j \, \alpha^{i-j} x_j + i \sum_{j=i+1}^n \alpha^{j-i} x_j, \qquad i = 1, \dots, n.
\]
The vector \(x\) lies in the kernel of \(A\) if and only if \(s_i = 0\) for all \(i\).

Introduce the auxiliary quantities \(q_{n+1} = 0\) and
\[
q_i = x_i + \alpha q_{i+1}, \qquad i = n, \dots, 1
\]
(equivalently, \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\) for \(i = 1, \dots, n\)). These satisfy
\[
q_i = \sum_{j=i}^n \alpha^{j-i} x_j.
\]
The tail sum in the expression for \(s_i\) then simplifies to \(\sum_{j > i} \alpha^{j-i} x_j = \alpha q_{i+1}\), so that
\[
s_i = \sum_{j=1}^i j \, \alpha^{i-j} x_j + i \alpha q_{i+1}.
\]
Substitute \(x_j = q_j - \alpha q_{j+1}\) into the remaining sum. After collecting coefficients of the \(q_k\), the cross terms involving \(q_{i+1}\) cancel and one obtains
\[
s_i = \sum_{k=1}^i \bigl( k - (k-1)\beta \bigr) \alpha^{i-k} \, q_k.
\]
Denote \(c_k = k - (k-1)\beta\) and
\[
u_i = \sum_{k=1}^i c_k \, \alpha^{i-k} q_k.
\]
The equation \(Ax = 0\) is then equivalent to \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i = 1, \dots, n\).

The quantities \(u_i\) satisfy the forward recurrence
\[
u_i - \alpha u_{i-1} = c_i q_i \qquad (i \geq 2),
\]
with the convention \(u_0 = 0\). In particular,
\[
u_1 = c_1 q_1, \qquad c_1 = 1.
\]
Thus \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i\) forces \(c_i q_i = 0\) for all \(i = 1, \dots, n\). Conversely, if \(c_k q_k = 0\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, n\), then the recurrence together with \(u_1 = 0\) implies \(u_i = 0\) for all \(i\) by induction. Consequently, \(Ax = 0\) if and only if \(c_k q_k = 0\) for all \(k\), where the sequence \((q_i)\) determines \(x\) via \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\) and \(q_{n+1} = 0\).

A nontrivial kernel exists precisely when there exists a nontrivial sequence \((q_1, \dots, q_n)\) with \(q_{n+1} = 0\) satisfying \(q_k = 0\) whenever \(c_k \neq 0\) (the values \(q_k\) may be chosen freely at those indices where \(c_k = 0\)). Solving \(c_k = 0\) yields
\[
k - (k-1)\beta = 0 \iff \beta = \frac{k}{k-1}
\]
for integers \(k \geq 2\) (the case \(k = 1\) gives \(c_1 = 1 \neq 0\) independently of \(\beta\)). Therefore:

- If \(\beta = m/(m-1)\) for some integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\), then \(c_m = 0\). Choosing, for example, \(q_m = 1\) and \(q_k = 0\) for all \(k \neq m\) produces a nontrivial sequence \((q_i)\). The corresponding vector \(x\) (given by \(x_i = q_i - \alpha q_{i+1}\)) is necessarily nonzero. Hence the kernel is nontrivial and \(A\) is singular.
- If \(\beta \neq m/(m-1)\) for every integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\), then \(c_k \neq 0\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, n\). The conditions \(c_k q_k = 0\) force \(q_k = 0\) for all \(k\), whence \(x = 0\). The kernel is trivial and \(A\) is nonsingular.

It follows that \(A\) is singular if and only if
\[
\alpha^2 = \frac{m}{m-1}
\]
for some integer \(m = 2, \dots, n\). Since \(\alpha > 0\), the positive values of \(a\) are exactly
\[
a_m = \sqrt{\frac{m}{m-1}}, \qquad m = 2, 3, \dots, 2026.
\]
These \(2025\) numbers are pairwise distinct. Their sum is
\[
\sum_{m=2}^{2026} \sqrt{\frac{m}{m-1}} = \sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}.
\]

For each such value the corresponding auxiliary sequence \((q_i)\) produces a nonzero vector \(x\) satisfying \(Ax = 0\), so the indicated values of \(a\) indeed render \(A\) singular. No other positive values of \(a\) produce a nontrivial kernel.

Thus the required sum is \(\sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}\).

Final answer: \(\sum_{k=1}^{2025} \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k}}\)
